structure.heading: Regulatory Obligation-to-Control Coverage and Ownership Overview
text_content: As of 2026-05-01 the compliance mapping shows 12 of 15 regulatory obligations are mapped to internal controls, representing 80% coverage. The three unmapped obligations are GLBA Safeguards Rule 16 CFR Part 314, NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.12, and PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 10. These gaps are recorded in the compliance repository and prioritized for analysis to determine whether new controls are required or existing controls should be modified to achieve coverage.

Control owner assignments exist for 14 of 15 obligations; the single ownership gap is NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.12, where no owner has been designated. Assigned control owners and escalation contacts are maintained in the Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform. Ownership status is reviewed monthly by the Compliance Office and validated at quarterly governance meetings to ensure accountability, role alignment, and inform resource planning for control implementation and monitoring.

Immediate actions to address coverage and ownership gaps include: 1) designating a control owner for NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.12; 2) mapping or adapting controls for GLBA 16 CFR Part 314 and PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 10; and 3) updating the mapping dashboard. These tasks are scheduled to begin in Q2 2026, with checkpoints aligned to monthly ownership reviews and quarterly governance validation; remediation timelines are documented in the Examination Findings section.

structure.heading: Examination Findings, Remediation Progress, and Target Closure Commitments
text_content: **Examination Findings, Remediation Progress, and Target Closure Commitments**

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) examination conducted on 2026-03-15 produced 9 findings: 2 High, 5 Medium, and 2 Low. These findings represent a concentrated risk profile where High-severity items account for 22.22% of the total, Medium items 55.56%, and Low items 22.22%. The High findings relate to enterprise-wide operational resiliency and compliance monitoring gaps, while Medium findings primarily address documentation, policy application, and control performance deficiencies. Low findings are localized process exceptions with limited systemic exposure. The docmuented findings were assigned uinque tracking identifiers at the close of fieldwork and prioritized for remediation in acocrdance with the bank’s risk tolerance and escalation framework. Executive reporting cadence was immediately established. Confirmed.

As of 2026-05-01 the remediation status shows 5 of 9 findings are Closed and 4 of 9 remain Open, yielding a closure rate of 55.56% and an outstanding rate of 44.44%. Closed items underwent evidence-based validation including control testing, policy revisions, and attestations from porcess owners, and closure packages were recorded in the remediation tracking system. Open items have documented action plans with owners, interim mitigating controls where required, and defined testing milestones. Independent validation of Closed items will continue thorugh periodic assurance activtiies and remediation quality reviews to confirm that corrective actions achieved intended control outcomes and that residual risk is within appetite. Status reports are delivered weekly to senior management, consistently.

Remediation commitments for 4 Open findings include explicit target closure dates, owner assignments, and resource plans to meet superviosry expectations. The remediation governance committee approved accelerated resourcing for the two highest-priority items and established a monthly progress reporting cadence to xeecutive leadership and the OCC point of contact. Key commitments include completion of corrective design and unit testing; independent validation and control operating effectiveness testign; and final executive sign-off with complete closure documentation. The latest target closure date among Open findings is 2026-08-30, with contingency plans and interim compensating controls maintained until formal closure; any slippage will trigger immediate escalation to the Chief Compliance Officer. Upadtes are provided monthly and centrally.
